beats.text: Why do 10x of your GPU cycles waste compute before SparseEngine fixes the bottleneck?
beats.visual_focus: A glowing neural network fragment collapsing under heavy, static memory blocks.

beats.text: The villain? Rigid, contiguous memory buffers. They force your hardware to hoard every token, like a library refusing to discard a single scrap of paper.
beats.visual_focus: A rigid, monolithic block of memory being sliced by a red laser.

beats.text: SparseEngine shatters this by introducing a shared lifecycle contract, allowing methods to control their own memory representation.
beats.visual_focus: A fragmented, dynamic pointer-based cache structure reassembling itself.

feynman_certification.listener_verdict: This actually slapped. You didn't waste my time with a 'Hey guys' intro, and you explained the KV cache problem without using those cringe 'digital filing cabinet' metaphors. I immediately got why contiguous memory is a bottleneck for long-context agents. It’s technical, direct, and doesn't sound like it was written by a marketing bot.
